It is submitted that the petitioner's appeal against the said conviction and sentence, i.e., CRL.A. 709/2003 was dismissed by a learned Division Bench of this Court vide judgment dated 12.05.2009.
3.
It is submitted that the petitioner has undergone more than 22 years of the sentence awarded to him.

It is submitted that the petitioner's application seeking grant of 1st spell of furlough was rejected by the competent authority, vide order no. F.10(003472148)/CJ/Legal/2024/3690 dated 12.01.2024, stating as under:
"In this regard, I am directed to inform you that the Competent Authority has considered the application for grant of furlough and same has been declined this stage as per Rule 1239 of Delhi Prison Rules-2018 in view of punishment dated 28.10.2023(Warning) has been issued for one day late surrender from furlough on 28.10.2023.

* Also, as per standing order No. 01/2019 "if a convict avails furlough regularly and happens to commit jail offence and a warning is recorded against him,
then he may be eligible for furlough after a gap of one year in case the jail offence committed by the said convict is minor."
4.
It is submitted that the petitioner has been released on parole/furlough on multiple occasions and each time, he has surrendered without misusing the liberty granted to him.
It is further pointed out that the jail conduct of the petitioner in the last one year has been satisfactory, except for the one punishment ticket awarded to him.
It is submitted that the petitioner got late by one day in surrendering on account of a delay in train timings, which was a circumstance out of his control.

sentences.text: In totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, the present petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to be released on furlough for a period on three weeks from the date of his release, subject to the following conditions:
i.
The petitioner shall furnish a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 10,000/- with one surety of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the concerned Jail Superintendent.
ii. The memo of parties reflects that the petitioner resides at Village Kapsona, Post Office and PS Shahkund, District Bhagalpur, Bihar.

In case of any change in address,
the petitioner is directed to

iii. The petitioner shall report to the SHO, PS Shahkund, once a week, on every Tuesday at 10:00 AM.
The concerned officer shall release the petitioner by 11:00 AM, after recording his presence completion of all necessary formalities.
iv. The petitioner shall not leave India during the period of parole.
v. The petitioner shall furnish his mobile number to the concerned jail authorities and to the Investigating Officer and keep it operational at all times.
vi. The petitioner shall not try to contact the family of the victim in any manner and shall not go in the vicinity of their residence at any time.
vii. The petitioner shall surrender before the concerned jail authorities immediately upon the expiry of his parole.
